summary: This paper demonstrates compilation of quantum error correction recovery rules directly into fixed open-loop control pulses for transmon circuits, using conditional transition frequencies as a control resource. In a four-qubit repetition-code ring, the resulting input-independent waveform protects logical coherence under Pauli-X noise and logical population under amplitude damping, with a scalable two-color scheduling architecture.
motivation: Conventional quantum error correction requires syndrome measurement, classical decoding, and measurement-conditioned feedback, creating overhead in readout fidelity, latency, and control routing. This work explores measurement-free QEC by compiling the joint syndrome selection and recovery into a single fixed waveform, leveraging spectral selectivity of coupled transmons.
method: The approach uses capacitive couplings between transmons to generate data-state-dependent frequency shifts on an auxiliary qubit. A two-stage composite drive—first a dual-tone photon-number-conserving swap, then a conditional two-photon 0↔2 transition on the auxiliary—addresses only the syndrome-selected data configurations while leaving others undriven. The local module is then pipelined across a four-site ring using a two-color bipartite schedule that avoids sideband crosstalk.
result: For the four-bit ring, the compiled waveform maps both error-syndrome-indicated computational basis inputs to their corrected targets with high fidelity (Figure 3(c)), and repeated cycles slow the decay of logical coherence C_Y by a factor ~2 under 30 μs^{-1} Pauli-X dephasing and stabilize the logical-one population P_1^L under 30 μs T₁ amplitude damping relative to unrecovered encoded states.
